subject: Capacity SOS: FastFin sustained saturation & reserved throughput shortfall — decisions needed
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fastfin.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency and 5xx spike — seeing reserved pool limits

Hannah / Marissa,

We started seeing sustained 99th percentile latency increases around 08:45 PT this morning across our main inference route. A subset of requests are 5xx'ing (502/504) and throughput is capped despite our reserved commit. This is hitting our fraud detection jobs (batch window).

Quick facts:
- Region: us-west-2
- Impact: elevated p99 from ~280ms -> ~1.2s, 5xx rate ~1.6% (was ~0.02%)
- Reserved throughput reported in the dashboard shows a hard ceiling at ~65k tokens/min, while traffic is at ~78k tokens/min

We need immediate help — can you confirm whether this is an internal pool saturation or routing fallback? This is impacting our nightly batch and will materially affect our SLA metrics for the month.

Can we get an ops contact on a short bridge?

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Ops, FastFin

--
Elena Morales
Elena.Morales@fastfin.com

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — seeing reserved pool limits

On Wed, Oct 7, 2026 at 09:40 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena — we’ll aim to get a 15m bridge up within 20 minutes and follow with a short action plan.
>
Quick diagnostic summary (ops):
- Observed: GPU headroom in FastFin's dedicated pool dropped from ~28% -> ~6% between 08:20-08:50 PT. Concurrently, prefix KV cache hit-rate for their hot route dropped from 84% -> 42%.
- Cause hypothesis: a sudden workload with longer sequence lengths plus a small number of large LLM generations exhausted persistent worker slot allocation and caused request queueing. Automatic routing attempted to spill to compatible hosted variants BUT those variants are running throttles under cross-tenant contention resulting in 502 errors.

Immediate mitigations attempted (10:00-10:10 PT):
- Increased per-tenant worker pool for FastFin by +2 nodes (temporary) — limited effect due to contiguous GPU memory pressure.
- Evicted low-priority batch jobs (best-effort) — reclaimed ~9% headroom.
- Applied aggressive KV-cache priming for most-frequent prefixes — improved hit-rate to ~60% but still below steady-state.

Suggested urgent options (we need exec sign-off for cost/impact):
A) Emergency short-term burst to a warm spare cluster (adds spend and needs infra green-light) — estimated 6 hours to fully provision (~$Xk/hr).
B) Graceful temporary model variant downgrade on non-critical endpoints to a quantized Llama-variant to reduce memory footprint (possible quality regression).
C) Route throttling on non-critical routes + token-based queuing (customer-visible rate limiting)

Attachments: throughput-dashboard.png (10:00 snapshot), kv-cache-hit-rates.csv (last 24h).

I’m on standby on the bridge.

— Vivek
VP, Runtime & Operations
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fastfin.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — seeing reserved pool limits

Hannah / Marissa,

This is unacceptable. We pay for reserved throughput and an SLA. We are in the middle of an important risk-detection batch and cannot have degraded quality or throttling. We want:
- Immediate mitigation so our jobs finish within the batch window.
- Clear root-cause and timeline for full remediation.
- Preliminary notice on any credits for SLA impact.

Can you confirm whether option A (emergency burst) is feasible immediately? If not, we need a timeline for B with expected precision delta vs. current model.

Samir Gupta
CTO, FastFin
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: samir.gupta@fastfin.com, elena.morales@fastfin.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec decision requested: fastfin emergency burst vs graceful degradation

Team — looping leadership for an urgent decision. Summary for execs:
- FastFin's dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 is at sustained saturation; headroom ~6%.
- Automatic spillover to hosted variants caused 502/504s under cross-tenant contention. Customer-facing 5xx rate peaked at ~1.6% and p99 latency >1s.
- We can: (A) provision emergency burst capacity to a warm spare cluster (~6h to full scale, immediate failover possible via routing; cost: high, temporary); or (B) perform a controlled model variant downgrade and token-throttling to reduce memory pressure (lower cost, potential quality regression and customer dissatisfaction).

Customer asks for immediate finish of batch window and SLA credit conversation. Marissa — please hold the line on credits/contract. David/Vivek — we need a quick binary decision: authorize emergency burst (ops to provision) OR approve immediate variant downgrade + short-term throttling. If we choose burst, finance needs to sign off on the spend and infra must confirm start time.

Proposed immediate action: authorize burst for 6 hours while ops works on a longer-term remediation (model optimization + prewarmed workers). If we cannot get finance sign-off within 30 minutes, fall back to option B with careful comms.

I’ll escalate to Sales/Finance leadership if there’s hesitation — customer is putting this on the exec timeline.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
